rationale: structural: `requirements.test-coverage.index.details` states only observable output behavior. The first clause is: "`habeas mdbook` MUST NOT generate per-test coverage subchapters or captured-source pages under the execution-coverage chapter". The second is: "File-notes pages supporting coverage gap explanations ... MUST remain available". Neither clause names a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. I tested each clause against a behavior-preserving alternative: - The generator could omit those pages by never creating them, by filtering them out after creation, or by running a different generator module. The book output is the same in each case, and the text allows all three. - File-notes pages could be produced by any code path, as long as they exist. `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` describes what those pages show, and that is behavior too. So no clause fixes how the implementation is built, and no implementation root needs an `{impl}` reference. The supplied review roots are empty, which is consistent with this. The context requirement `requirements.test-coverage.index` only requires one documented-coverage-gaps subchapter to be generated, and that is also an output requirement. It checks that the pages nested under the coverage chapter have the right parent names and section numbers, that they link back to `../coverage.html`, and that they have no source path. - It runs with the index both numbered and unnumbered.
